g12-ch1-board-03.a: Equivalence relation; the class of $P$ is the circle with centre $O$ and radius $OP$.
g12-ch1-board-03.s: $OP=OP$ [1]. $OP=OQ\Rightarrow OQ=OP$ [1]. $OP=OQ$, $OQ=OS\Rightarrow OP=OS$ [1]. $Q$ is related to $P\iff OQ=OP$ [1], the circle with centre $O$ and radius $OP$ [1].

alt.q: $A=\{1,2,\dots,7\}$ and $aRb\iff a,b$ are both odd or both even. Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation and write its classes.
alt.s: Same parity is reflexive [1], symmetric [1] and transitive [1]. Classes: odd numbers and even numbers [2].

g12-ch1-board-03.q: Case study. A company gives each of its $5$ employees an ID from $I=\{101,102,\dots,108\}$; different employees get different IDs. Let $f$ map each employee to the ID. (i) Is $f$ one-one? [1] (ii) Is $f$ onto $I$? [1] (iii) In how many ways can the IDs be given? [2] \textbf{OR} (iii) If only IDs $101$ to $105$ are used, how many bijections are possible? [2]
g12-ch1-board-03.s: (i) Different employees, different IDs [1]. (ii) $5$ images cannot cover $8$ IDs [1]. (iii) ${}^8P_5=8\cdot7\cdot6\cdot5\cdot4$ [1] $=6720$ [1]. OR $5!$ [1] $=120$ [1].
